answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidder to lock a fixed bond for every active job, releasing it only when a public verifier accepts the result and slashing it after an invalid result or missed deadline. Through this prism, a fresh name carries no trust signal beyond its bond; a claimed history is just a fable. Creating names stays cheap, but occupying 1,000 job slots requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and risking its loss on failed work.
